body.statement: Along the retained even tail \(n\ge N_0\), for every fixed finite \(\gamma\ge0\), \(\bigl(D_n(W_{n,\mathrm{stop}}),E_n(W_{n,\mathrm{stop}})\bigr)\Rightarrow(C_{k,a},\varepsilon)\), where \(C_{k,a}\) and \(\varepsilon\) are independent. Hence \(\|C_{k,a}\|^2=\min\{\chi_k^2,a\}\), with boundary mass \(1-\Pr(\chi_k^2\le a)\); consequently, for finite \(a\), this law is not the classical uniform-rerandomization law \(L_{k,a}\), which gives the boundary sphere probability zero. The law of \(H\) may depend on \(\gamma\), but the displayed terminal law does not.
body.justification: The radial boundary component and pathwise residual independence are the design-specific features hidden by stationary or conditional approximations.
body.gap: Classical Mahalanobis rerandomization yields a Gaussian conditioned inside the ball; no located result derives the radial first-entry clipping law for original PSRR.
body.consumer: The explicit endpoint law permits direct power, variance, and critical-value calculations for a design that currently has only Fisher sharp-null inference.
